newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.05 pct after drain.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.05 pct after drain.

text.p: German call money rates traded mostly steady around 3.05 percent in calm dealings on Wednesday even though the Bundesbank drained funds from the system at this week's repo tender allocation.

The bulk of trades again occured at 3.05 percent with the range of trades moving between three and 3.10 percent, dealers said, adding that rates were expected to stabilise near the three percent level over the next sessions.
The Bundesbank this morning alloted 64.3 billion marks in repos at a fixed three percent rate to replace an expiring 65 billion mark repo pact.
Although dealers had mostly expected the Bundesbank to fully replace the expiring repo pact, they said the 700 million mark drain would not significantly impact rates in coming sessions.
"After seeing the reserve data, the drain was justified," one chief dealer at a major Frankfurt bank said.
Others added this week's movement was not overly dramatic and should help maintain the status quo, where rates do not fluctuate wildly, mostly hovering near the repo rate level.
Apart from the tender allocation, there were talking points for the market, dealers said.
Banks' holdings at the Bundesbank stood at 38.5 billion marks on Tuesday, while average holdings on a month-to-date basis stood at 38.4 billion marks.
Lombard borrowings totalled about 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rate was set at 3.09033 percent on Wednesday compared with 3.09667 percent on Tuesday.
